subject.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access

question: How should an upgrade handle existing trigger-script cron jobs whose creator-derived tool cap was never recorded and cannot be reconstructed?
rationale: Preserving these rows leaves the shipped escalation path active, while disabling them can interrupt legitimate unrestricted operator jobs; source evidence cannot choose that security-versus-compatibility policy safely.

options.title: Quarantine Legacy Triggers
options.body: Disable evaluation for cap-less legacy trigger scripts until an operator reviews and re-saves each job with an explicit approved policy.

options.title: Accept Forward-Only Hardening
options.body: Merge the PR as written and explicitly accept that existing cap-less jobs remain unrestricted until operators audit or edit them.

options.title: Design Provenance First
options.body: Hold the PR while maintainers design a broader migration or provenance mechanism that can classify legacy jobs without stopping them all.

recommendation.title: Quarantine Legacy Triggers
recommendation.body: Disable evaluation for cap-less legacy trigger scripts until an operator reviews and re-saves each job with an explicit approved policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent authorization and cron-runtime history most directly spans the security and compatibility surfaces requiring this decision.
